newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close higher, securities firms lead.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close higher, securities firms lead.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed higher on Thursday, led by a broad-based rebound in shares of securities firms and banks, brokers said.
The Japanese yen's overnight rise in London boosted buying in shipbuilders and export sectors, but the impact waned later with the currency's decline in Tokyo.
The composite index gained 1.16 percent, or 8.87 points, to close at 774.66.
"This is a continuation from a recent rally driven by ample liquidity after fears over futures-linked selling fizzled," said Shim Choong-bo, research manager at Daishin Securities.
The yen was trading at 114.25/35 per dollar in Tokyo, down from 110.62 reached in London.

Securities firms soared in a rebound from the recent drops on profit-taking. The sector's sub-index jumped 7.02 percent, or 103.87 points, to 1,582.68 as investors bet the low interest rates would help boost earnings at brokerage houses.

Most securities firms rose to their daily limits. Daewoo Securities gained 1,300 won to its limit and yearly high of 17,600. LG Securities also ended at its upper limit and yearly high of 14,300 won by rising 1,000 won.
Midopa Department Store gained 580 won to its limit of 7,890 after the company announced that it would sell its loss-making construction division to another company.
Midopa said the sales were part of the self-rescue plan now being promoted by its parent Dainong Group, which was tapped in May for bail-out by its creditor banks.
The market was little affected by the Securities Supervisory Board's plan to form special teams to investigate announcements by listed firms that could seriously influence share prices.
